name: Nasserism
summary: Nasserism is the Arab nationalist and Arab socialist outlook of Gamal Abdel Nasser's Egypt: pan-Arab unity, anti-imperialism and non-alignment, state-led industrialization, nationalization and land reform, and class collaboration in place of class struggle. It was carried out through a one-party, army-led corporatist state around a charismatic leader, with religion treated as a marker of Arab identity to be contained rather than as a basis of government.
scope: Nasser's Egypt of 1952-1970 as scholars describe the ideology: its pan-Arab, étatist-socialist, corporatist, militarist and secular-nationalist pillars (Şahin; Encyclopedia.com), Nasser's Philosophy of the Revolution and the 1962 National Charter. Answers rest on the regime's record where one exists and otherwise on its stated doctrine. Later Nasserist parties under Sadat, Mubarak and after (Hamdeen Sabahi's current) and Latin American 'Nasserist' military regimes are other subjects and are not used.
notes: Themes searched: economy, government, world, society, religion, means. Many statements stay null because the defining sources describe only the regime's economic, political and foreign record. Not opened: Britannica's Nasserism entry (403/404), the SOAS chapter 'Nasserism' (bot check), Ajami 1974 and Mansfield 1973 (paywalled). Present-day Nasserists' views on democracy are not Nasser-era doctrine and are left out.
